name: field
title: Field
summary: Frames one control with what a form gives every field: a label above it that can say the control is required or optional, a line of help, and the reason a value was refused, each tied to the control for assistive technology; it is a frame, never a control.

anatomy.description: Names the control: above it, from the start edge, still, and never cut. The requirement mark follows it. Left out where the control draws the label itself, floating in its own box (FLD-25).
A glyph of the icon set before the label, decorative to assistive technology.
After the label: the Tag component at its small size, drawn as every small tag is and never a control, saying the control is required or optional; or, for required, an asterisk after the label.

The control's present value in words, at the end of the label row: for a control whose value cannot be read from the control itself (a slider). Words the field is given; it never reads or formats a value.

The one control the field frames: a control that has no label, help and error of its own (a slider, a switch, a control the product built). It keeps its own tokens, states, keyboard, events and value; the field gives it a name, a description, and its required, invalid and disabled states.

A line of help below the control, from where the control's content starts (FLD-26), It stays while the field is in error, with the error text below it. No row is drawn, and no room kept, while there is neither a help, an error text nor a count.

The reason the value was refused, in words, in the supporting row: in the help's place, directly below the control, or below the help, which stays, where comp.field.error-text.placement is append (FLD-7, FLD-31). Drawn only while the field is in error; no room is kept for it before.

A count about the control's value, in the words the field is given (countText) — a text input's characters typed and, after a slash, the most allowed — at the end of the supporting row's first line (FLD-27). The field draws it and does not count.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the control, visibly and to assistive technology. Required, unless the control names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label): then leave it empty and the field adds only help and an error.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Does not draw the label, which stays the accessible name. For a control whose visible label is elsewhere (a table column, a toolbar).

props.name: supportingText
props.description: Help shown below the control and given to assistive technology as the control's description. While the field is in error it gives way to errorText, unless the design system keeps both (comp.field.error-text.placement append).

props.name: errorText
props.description: Shown while error is true, in supportingText's place — or below it, which then stays, where the design system's comp.field.error-text.placement is append: what is wrong and how to put it right, in words.

props.name: error
props.description: Puts the field in the error condition: the error text is drawn, the control is exposed as invalid and, where it has an error condition of its own, drawn in it. What a value means is the product's to validate; the field never sets this itself.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control and draws the frame as disabled. Disable a framed control here, not on the control, so that its label follows.

props.name: required
props.description: What the form asks of the control: true exposes it as required and draws the required mark beside the label. It never validates: a missing answer is the product's to report with error.

props.name: optional
props.description: Draws the optional tag after the label and adds optionalText to the control's description, because assistive technology has no state for it. Ignored while required is true: a control is never both.

props.name: requiredMark
props.description: How this control shows that it is required: tag is a small filled Tag with requiredText, asterisk is "*" after the label, none draws nothing and keeps the semantics. Auto takes comp.field.requirement.mark, which follows sys.behavior.requirement-mark, the system's one answer. Ignored unless required is true.

props.name: requiredText
props.description: The text of the required tag, in the product's language ("Required", "必須"). The product's: Tanrei has no word for it. Empty reads the product's words; with neither, FLD-24 says what is drawn.

props.name: optionalText
props.description: The text of the optional tag, in the product's language ("Optional", "任意"); also read to assistive technology as part of the description. The product's: Tanrei has no word for it. Empty reads the product's words.

props.name: countText
props.description: A count about the control's value, as it is to be drawn ("12/40"), at the end of the supporting row. For a control that keeps a count (a text input whose counter is true). The product's, or the composed component's that holds the field; kept from assistive technology, because the control says its own count.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The control's present value in words ("40 %", "$100 – $300"), drawn at the end of the label row. For a control whose value cannot be read from the control itself (a slider). The product's, or the composed component's that holds the field; kept from assistive technology, because the control says its own value.

items.name: slider
items.summary: A Slider as the field's control: the slider component, named, described and disabled by the field, otherwise drawn and behaving as it does anywhere.

props.name: value
props.description: Its value, as the Slider's value.

items.name: switch
items.summary: A Switch as the field's control, with no label of its own: the field's label names it.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether it is on, as the Switch's checked.

items.name: checkbox
items.summary: A Checkbox as the field's control. It names itself with its own label, so the field's label is left empty and the field adds help and an error.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether it is on, as the Checkbox's checked.

props.name: label
props.description: Its own label, drawn beside the box, as the Checkbox's label.

items.name: one-time-code-input
items.summary: A One-time-code input as the field's control, with no label of its own: the field names it, describes it and puts it in its error condition.

props.name: value
props.description: The code entered so far, as the One-time-code input's value.

props.name: groupSize
props.description: How many cells a group has, as the One-time-code input's groupSize.

items.name: file-upload
items.summary: A File upload as the field's control, in its button layout and with no label of its own: the field's label names its group, and the field's help, error and requirement join the description of its trigger (FUP-32). The item's content is the label of the trigger, the product's own Button.

props.name: constraintsText
props.description: The limits in words, as the File upload's constraintsText: drawn below the trigger, and still read while the field shows its error.

items.name: file-picker
items.summary: A File picker as the field's control, in its button layout and with no label of its own: the field's label names its group, and the field's help, error and requirement join the description of its trigger (FPK-21). The item's content is the label of the trigger, the product's own Button.

props.name: constraintsText
props.description: The limits in words, as the File picker's constraintsText: drawn below the trigger, and still read while the field shows its error.

props.name: selectionText
props.description: What is chosen now, in the product's words, as the File picker's selectionText: beside the trigger.

items.name: text-input
items.summary: A Text input as the field's control: the pair a text field is. The field names it, describes it and puts it in its error condition; the input says back what only it knows — that it draws the label itself, where its text starts and ends, an entry error (FLD-25, FLD-26, FLD-28).

props.name: entries
props.description: What was entered already: each string is drawn as one small input Chip in the Text input's entries slot (TXI-64), in order — disabled while the field is, and without its remove action while the input is read-only. A product writes these chips by hand; a chip field makes them from its value.

props.name: entryRemoveLabel
props.description: The accessible name of each entry's remove action, with {entry} standing for the entry's text ("Remove {entry}"): what a product writes on each chip by hand as the Chip's removeLabel.

places.name: entry
places.description: The text of the entry the action removes.

items.name: number-input
items.summary: A Number input as the field's control: the pair a number field is. The field names it, describes it and puts it in its error condition; the input says back what only it knows — that it draws the label itself, where its number's line starts and ends, a text that is not a number (FLD-25, FLD-26, FLD-28).

items.name: color-input
items.summary: A Color input as the field's control: the pair a color field is. The field names it, describes it and puts it in its error condition; the input says back what only it knows — that it draws the label itself, where the value's text starts, after its swatch, and an entry error (FLD-25, FLD-26, FLD-28).

items.name: select
items.summary: A Select as the field's control: the pair a select field is. The field names it, describes it and puts it in its error condition; the select says back what only it knows — that it draws the label itself in a look that floats one, where its value starts and ends, and that its list is open (FLD-13, FLD-25, FLD-26). In a fixture, an item of this kind holds the select's own options as its items and fills the select's own slots.

items.name: combobox
items.summary: A Combobox as the field's control: the pair a combobox field is. The field names it, describes it and puts it in its error condition; the combobox says back what only it knows — that it draws the label itself in a look that floats one, where its input text starts and ends, and that its list is open (FLD-13, FLD-25, FLD-26). In a fixture, an item of this kind holds the combobox's own options as its items and fills the combobox's own slots.

items.name: chat-composer
items.summary: A Chat composer as the field's control, with no label of its own: the field's label names it and its typing area, the field's help and, in error, its error text are the last part of the typing area's description, and the field's error and disabled are the composer's (CCM-28). The composer draws its own capsule and none of the field's rows.

props.name: sendLabel
props.description: As the Chat composer's sendLabel: the name of its send button, which the field does not give (CCM-31).

behavior.text: THE field SHALL lay out, from top to bottom and from its start edge: its label row (FLD-2), its control comp.field.label.gap below the last line of that row, and its supporting row (FLD-7) comp.field.supporting-text.gap below the control. It SHALL be as wide as its layout gives it and give the control that whole width to lay itself out in — a control that fills the width it is given fills it, and a control with a size of its own keeps it, at the start edge — and SHALL be as tall as its rows and its control together. THE field SHALL draw no container, edge, fill or elevation of its own, SHALL add no padding around its rows, and SHALL NOT change the size, the look or the behaviour of its control.
behavior.verify: Under the default system: a one-line label (20), 8, the control, 4, one line of supporting text (16). The same label, gaps and supporting line as the fixture stacked-supporting of the text field, to the pixel, when the two are drawn at one width.

behavior.text: WHILE label is not empty, labelHidden is false and its control does not draw the label itself (FLD-25) THE field SHALL draw label above its control, from the field's start edge, in comp.field.label.typescale and comp.field.standard.label.color (comp.field.standard.error.label.color WHILE error is true). The label SHALL keep its place, size and style whatever the control holds, SHALL wrap onto as many lines as it needs, and SHALL never be cut with an ellipsis or drawn over the control, because text enlarged to 200% must lose no content. WHILE labelHidden is true or label is empty THE field SHALL draw neither the label row nor the gap below it, and SHALL draw no label glyph and no requirement mark (FLD-3, FLD-6).
behavior.verify: Unit: in a field 96 wide a label that needs two lines draws both, above the control, and the control starts 8 below the second.

behavior.text: WHILE the label is drawn and the label-icon slot holds a glyph THE field SHALL draw it before the label, comp.field.label-icon.gap from it, at comp.field.label-icon.size, centred on the label's first line, with sys.icon.family.unselected and sys.icon.fill.unselected, sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max, in comp.field.standard.label-icon.color (comp.field.standard.error.label-icon.color WHILE error is true), and SHALL keep it from assistive technology, because the label names the control; WHILE the label is not drawn THE field SHALL NOT draw the label glyph and SHALL report it in debug builds.

THE field SHALL take from required and optional what the form asks of its control: WHILE required is true it exposes the control as required (FLD-10) and draws the required mark (FLD-5, FLD-6); WHILE optional is true it draws the optional tag (FLD-5) and adds optionalText to the control's description (FLD-11), because assistive technology has no state for it; WHILE both are false it says nothing and draws nothing. THE field SHALL NOT validate because of required: it SHALL NOT set the error condition for a missing value or show an error text of its own; what a missing value means is the product's to say with error and errorText. WHILE disabled is true THE field SHALL keep its mark: an asterisk drawn from the field's disabled tokens (FLD-14), a requirement tag drawn as a tag inside something disabled (FLD-5, TAG-21).
behavior.verify: Unit: required true sets the required state on the control and never the invalid state; optional adds optionalText to the description (the fixtures give "Optional") and no required state.

behavior.text: WHILE the label is drawn and optional is true, or required is true and the required mark is tag (FLD-6), THE field SHALL draw after the label's text, comp.field.requirement.gap from it and centred on the label's last line, a requirement tag: the Tag component, drawn as every tag is — size small, variant filled for required and tonal for optional, status default, no glyph and no dot, its label requiredText or optionalText on one line (TAG-1, TAG-2, TAG-5) — from the Tag's own tokens (comp.tag.container.height.small, comp.tag.label.typescale.small, comp.tag.filled.container.color, comp.tag.tonal.container.color and the others those sentences name). THE field SHALL have no token for the requirement tag's fill, lettering, text style, paddings or corners and SHALL set none of the Tag's for it, so that a design system or a product that restyles its small tags restyles the requirement tag with them and nothing restyles the requirement tag alone. THE field SHALL draw the requirement tag the same at rest, WHILE focus is inside the field and WHILE error is true, because a tag has no states (TAG-9) and what the form asks has not changed; WHILE disabled is true THE field SHALL have it drawn as a tag inside something disabled (TAG-21), from the Tag's own disabled tokens, so that the tag fades with the label it follows and no part of a disabled field reads as live. The requirement tag is text, never a control: it SHALL take no focus and no hover, focus or press answer of its own (a press on it does what a press on the label does, FLD-12). It SHALL NOT make the label's row taller: where it is taller than the label's line it SHALL reach equally above and below that line. WHEN the label and the requirement tag do not fit on one line THE field SHALL wrap the label (FLD-2) and move the tag whole to a line of its own after the label's last line, never cutting or splitting it. WHILE requiredText or optionalText is empty THE field SHALL NOT draw the tag of that kind and in debug builds SHALL report it. THE field SHALL keep the required tag from assistive technology, because the required state already says it, and SHALL give the optional tag's text as part of the description (FLD-4).
behavior.verify: Fixtures slider-required, slider-optional, slider-required-ja, slider-required-error, slider-required-disabled and slider-rtl. Unit: the label's row is as tall with the tag as without it; the tag is not in the accessibility tree while the control is exposed as required; the required and optional tags overlay the tag fixtures small-filled and small-tonal pixel for pixel under every shipped system, at rest and with error true, and with disabled true the tag fixtures small-filled-disabled and small-tonal-disabled; with comp.tag.container.shape and comp.tag.tonal.container.color set for the page the requirement tags change as every other small tag there does; the requirement tag's element carries no token of its own, and no token of comp.field names a tag's fill, lettering, text style, padding or corner.

behavior.text: WHILE required is true and the label is drawn THE field SHALL draw the required mark that requiredMark names — tag (FLD-5), asterisk or none — and WHILE requiredMark is auto, the one comp.field.requirement.mark names: that token follows sys.behavior.requirement-mark, the design system's one answer for every field and every set of controls, unless a layer gives comp.field.requirement.mark a value of its own. As asterisk it SHALL draw the character "*" after the label's text, comp.field.requirement.asterisk-gap from it, in the label's text style, in comp.field.standard.required-asterisk.color (comp.field.standard.error.required-asterisk.color WHILE error is true), and SHALL keep it from assistive technology, because the required state already says it; as none it SHALL draw no mark and still expose the required state. WHILE the label is not drawn THE field SHALL draw no mark, and SHALL still expose the required state and the optional description.
behavior.verify: Fixture slider-required-asterisk. Under the default system the mark is tag. Unit: with sys.behavior.requirement-mark set to asterisk and to none a field under auto follows it; with comp.field.requirement.mark set against the system's choice the field's token wins; requiredMark tag, asterisk and none each win over both; requiredMark chip is an unknown value (FLD-22).

behavior.text: THE field SHALL draw its supporting row below the control, from the start edge of the control's content (FLD-26). It holds supportingText, the help, WHILE it is not empty, in comp.field.supporting-text.typescale and comp.field.standard.supporting-text.color (comp.field.standard.error.supporting-text.color WHILE the field is in error), and the error text WHILE the field is in error and has words for it (FLD-31). How the two share the row is the one comp.field.error-text.placement names. WHERE it is replace, its first value, THE field SHALL NOT draw the help WHILE it draws the error text, which stands in the help's place, because what the person must read then is what is wrong with the answer, and a field in error is no taller for it than at rest; WHEN the error text goes THE field SHALL draw the help again where it was. WHERE it is append THE field SHALL keep the help in its place and its words WHILE it draws the error text, and draw the error text below it, because the help says how to answer, which is what the person needs then. Each text SHALL wrap onto as many lines as it needs and never be cut. WHILE countText is not empty THE field SHALL draw it at the end of the row's first line (FLD-27). WHILE there is neither a help, an error text nor a count THE field SHALL draw neither the row nor its gap, and SHALL keep no room for it.
behavior.verify: A control with no box of its own has its content at the field's start edge, so the row starts there; a control that says where its content starts — a text input, drawn as a box — has the row start at its input text (FLD-26, TXI-62). Unit: the row appears and goes with its texts, and the field's height follows. Under the default system (replace) a field with a help and an error text holds the error text alone, in the help's place, and with error false again the help, where it was; with comp.field.error-text.placement set to append it holds both, the help first, and with error false again the help alone, where it was.

behavior.text: WHILE error is true THE field SHALL draw its label, its label glyph, its asterisk and its help from the error parts of its tokens (FLD-2, FLD-3, FLD-5 to FLD-7), SHALL draw its error text (FLD-31), SHALL expose its control as invalid to assistive technology, and SHALL put its control in the control's own error condition where the control has one (a checkbox's error), so that the control itself is marked and not only its text; a control with no error condition SHALL stay as it is drawn. THE field SHALL never set error itself: what a value means is the product's to validate. The one error it shows without it is its control's own refusal of an entry (FLD-28).
behavior.verify: Under the default system no part that was drawn before the error changes color — the label, the glyph, the requirement mark and the help keep their resting colors — and the error text alone takes the error role. Unit: a checkbox in a field with error true draws its error form and is exposed as invalid; a slider is exposed as invalid and drawn as before.

behavior.text: WHEN error becomes true, or errorText changes while error is true, and focus is inside the field THE field SHALL have assistive technology announce the shown error text once, politely; an error set while focus is elsewhere SHALL be read as part of the control's description when the control is next focused. THE field SHALL NOT move focus because of an error, and SHALL announce no other change of its texts: the help is not said again when the error appears, because it has not changed and is still read with the control (FLD-11).

THE field SHALL make label the accessible name of its control, whether or not the label is drawn (labelHidden), WHERE the control has no accessible name of its own; a control that names itself (a checkbox or a switch with its own label, a control the product named) SHALL keep that name, and WHERE such a control stands under a drawn label THE field SHALL in debug builds report that the control has two labels. WHILE label is empty and the control has no name of its own THE field SHALL still render and in debug builds report that the control has no accessible name. WHILE required is true THE field SHALL expose the control as required, whichever mark is drawn and where none is.
behavior.verify: Unit: the accessible name of a slider in a field is the field's label with labelHidden false and true; a checkbox with its own label in a field with an empty label keeps its name and nothing is reported.

behavior.text: THE field SHALL make these the description of its control, in this order, after any description the control has of its own and whether or not the label is drawn: supportingText, WHILE the row draws it (FLD-7); the error text WHILE the field is in error (FLD-31); optionalText WHILE optional is true — the order in which a field group describes its set (FGR-11). The description SHALL say what the row draws: WHERE comp.field.error-text.placement is replace, the error text in the help's place WHILE the field is in error; WHERE it is append, the help and then the error text. WHEN one of these texts comes, goes or changes THE field SHALL expose the new description at once. The label glyph, the required tag and the asterisk SHALL NOT be exposed.

WHEN the user presses the label, the label glyph or the requirement mark THE field SHALL move focus to its control and do nothing else: it SHALL NOT activate, switch or change the control, and SHALL draw no press answer, because a press on a label is not an action. A press on the supporting row SHALL do nothing. THE field SHALL add no stop to the focus order and handle no key: its control is the only thing in it that takes focus, and the control's own keys are the control's.

WHILE focus is inside the field — on its control or on any part of it, however the focus was gained — or its control says that it is drawn focused (for one, a select or a combobox for as long as its list is open) THE field SHALL draw its label, its label glyph, its asterisk, its value text and its supporting row from its focused tokens (their error parts WHILE error is true), as a text input's box does (TXI-6), so that a form shows which field has focus in one way for every field; the control draws its own focus indicator, and THE field SHALL draw none. WHEN focus enters or leaves, or error or disabled changes, THE field SHALL change its colors over comp.field.motion.state-duration with comp.field.motion.state-easing, and at once WHERE motion is reduced.
behavior.verify: Focused cannot be a snapshot fixture. Unit: focus the control by pointer and by keyboard and read the resolved tokens: under the default system the focused label takes the primary role, as a focused text field's does, and every other part keeps its resting color; with error true the label keeps its error color. The default system's primary is the surface's text color in every scheme, so the change shows only in a system whose primary is chromatic: test it with the m3-like preset.

behavior.text: WHILE disabled is true THE field SHALL draw every part of its own from its disabled tokens (of its error parts WHILE error is true) and its requirement tag as a tag inside something disabled (FLD-5, TAG-21), SHALL make its control disabled as that control's own disabled does — not focusable, not operable, exposed as disabled — and SHALL NOT answer a press on its label (FLD-12); WHILE disabled is false THE field SHALL NOT enable a control the product disabled itself. A disabled field SHALL keep its texts readable by assistive technology.

THE field SHALL frame exactly one control. IF it is given none THE field SHALL draw its rows without one and in debug builds report it; IF it is given more than one THE field SHALL lay them out in the order given, name, describe and mark only the first (FLD-8, FLD-10, FLD-11), and in debug builds report that a set of controls is a field group. IF its control is a component that has this frame already — a composed field, which is a Field and its one control (a text field, a select field) — THE field SHALL in debug builds report that the control is already a field and that the bare control is the one that field frames (for a text field, the text input), and SHALL hide neither frame.

WHILE the text size is enlarged THE field SHALL grow with its texts: the label and the supporting row wrap and never clip, the requirement tag grows with its text and keeps its paddings, the label glyph keeps comp.field.label-icon.size, the value text grows with its text and keeps the line FLD-29 gives it, and the rows keep their order and their gaps; at 200% no text SHALL be lost, lie over another part or need scrolling in two directions.

WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors (the web's forced-colors mode, and a platform's equivalent where it has one) THE field SHALL draw its label, its asterisk, its value text, its supporting text and its error text in the platform's text color and its requirement tag as a tag is drawn there (an edge and a label in the text color, TAG-14), and SHALL rely on no color of its own to tell an error from help: the error is carried by the words of errorText, by the invalid state (FLD-8) and by the control's own error condition; the two texts, drawn in one color there, are told apart by their words and their order, the help first.
behavior.verify: On the web, with forced colors emulated: every text of every fixture is CanvasText and each requirement tag has a visible edge.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE field SHALL mirror its layout: the label row, the control and the supporting row start at the right edge, the label glyph stands at the right of the label and the requirement mark at its left, and the value text stands at the left end of the label row.

THE field SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the field is shown THE field SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its control, with that control's value and focus.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE field SHALL draw the glyph of its label-icon slot mirrored left to right exactly when the system's icon set marks that glyph's name as mirrored or the product forces mirroring for that use, and unmirrored when the product forbids it: the icon helper mirrors the glyph inside its own box, about the box's vertical centre line, changing neither its place, size, color and fill nor the order FLD-18 gives. THE field SHALL NOT mirror a glyph itself, and SHALL NOT mirror content the product gives as an image or a view of its own rather than by a glyph's name.
behavior.verify: volume_up is marked by the default icon set; the fixture slider-rtl draws it mirrored, at the right of the label.

behavior.text: THE field SHALL lay out its label, its value text, its supporting text and error text and the text of its requirement tag as text of its own direction, isolated from the text around it: each takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right word, a number with its sign or unit, a telephone number and an address keep their own order in a right-to-left layout and reorder nothing beside them; THE field SHALL still place each and align its lines by the layout direction, not by the text's own.
WHEN requiredMark names a value the field does not know THE field SHALL behave as auto, and in debug builds THE field SHALL report the unknown value.

THE field SHALL leave its control what it is: the control keeps its own tokens, states, keyboard, events, value and place in a form, and THE field SHALL emit no event, hold no value and take no part in form submission. WHEN the control is replaced by another while the field is shown THE field SHALL name, describe and mark the new one (FLD-8, FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14) at once, and SHALL take back from the old one everything it gave it.

THE field SHALL have no words of its own: it SHALL take requiredText and optionalText from the instance's prop and, WHILE that is empty, from the product's words of the same name — the words a product sets once for all its components — and from nowhere else. IF neither gives requiredText WHILE required is true and the required mark is tag THE field SHALL draw the asterisk of FLD-6 in the tag's place, so that the requirement is still shown without a word, SHALL keep the required state on its control (FLD-10), and in debug builds SHALL report the missing words once. IF neither gives optionalText WHILE optional is true THE field SHALL draw no tag, SHALL add nothing to the description for it, and in debug builds SHALL report the missing words once.
behavior.verify: Unit, with no product's words set: required true and no requiredText draws the asterisk and no tag, and the report names requiredText; optional true and no optionalText draws no tag and adds nothing to the description. With the product's words set, an instance without the props draws them; an instance's own prop wins. No test finds an English word the test did not give.

behavior.text: WHILE its control draws the label itself — a control whose look floats its name inside its own box (for one, a text input of the filled or the outlined look, TXI-13) — THE field SHALL draw no label row, no gap below it, no label glyph and no requirement tag, as WHILE labelHidden is true (FLD-2), and SHALL still give the control label as its accessible name (FLD-10). With the name it SHALL give the control three things to draw the label by: whether labelHidden is true, so that the control draws none either; and the required mark, as an asterisk WHILE required is true and the mark FLD-6 names is tag or asterisk, and as none otherwise; and optionalText WHILE optional is true, because a person who sees the asterisk on the required fields of a form must also see which ones may be left out, and the optional tag of the label row has no room in a label that floats. The control draws both after the label's text, from its own tokens (for a text input, TXI-50). THE field SHALL keep its supporting row, its error condition, and the description and the states it gives (FLD-7 to FLD-11, FLD-14) unchanged. A press on a label the control draws is a press on the control, and the control's to answer (for a text input, TXI-8): FLD-12 speaks of the row the field draws. WHILE optional is true THE field SHALL keep optionalText in the description as well (FLD-11); WHILE the label-icon slot holds a glyph it SHALL report it as FLD-3 says. WHEN the control starts or stops drawing the label THE field SHALL leave out or draw its label row at once, without motion.
behavior.verify: Fixtures text-outlined-empty, text-filled-filled, text-outlined-required and text-outlined-label-hidden. Unit: a Field around a text input whose variant changes from stacked to outlined loses its label row and keeps the input's accessible name; requiredMark tag gives the input an asterisk; optional true gives it optionalText, which it draws after its floating label.

behavior.text: WHERE its control's content is inset from the control's own edges and the control says by how much — for one, a text input: from its start edge to where its text starts, past its inline padding and a leading icon, and the padding it keeps at its end edge (TXI-62) — THE field SHALL start its supporting row that far from its own start edge and end it that far before its end edge, so that the help and the error start where the text starts (FLD-7). The label row SHALL stay at the field's edges (FLD-2). A control that says nothing SHALL have the row at the field's edges, as a slider has. WHEN what the control says changes — its size, an icon that comes or goes, the layout direction — the row SHALL follow at once, without motion.
behavior.verify: Fixtures text-stacked-supporting and text-stacked-error: the supporting text starts at the input text, not at the label's edge. Unit: adding a leading icon to the text input moves the start of the row to the text; a slider's row is at the field's edge.

behavior.text: WHILE countText is not empty THE field SHALL draw it at the end of the supporting row's first line — beside the first line of the help, or of the error text WHILE there is no help — on one line that does not wrap, at least comp.field.counter.gap from every line of the help and of the error text, which both wrap in the room the count leaves beside it, and SHALL keep it in that place WHEN the error text comes or goes below a help, in comp.field.supporting-text.typescale with figures of equal width and in comp.field.standard.counter.color (comp.field.standard.error.counter.color WHILE the field is in error; their focused and disabled tokens as FLD-13 and FLD-14 say), and SHALL draw the row for the count alone WHILE there is no text to show. THE field SHALL draw the count as it is given and SHALL NOT count, format, describe or announce it, and SHALL keep the drawn count from assistive technology: countText is words the field is given — by the composed component that holds it (a text field gives its text input's count, TXF-67) or by the product that writes the pair by hand — about a control that makes the same count part of its own description and announces it (TXI-19). It SHALL lay the count out as text of its own direction (FLD-21), at the left end of the row in a right-to-left layout (FLD-18), in the platform's text color under forced colors (FLD-17), and WHILE the text size is enlarged SHALL keep it whole on its line while the text beside it wraps (FLD-16). A press on the count SHALL do nothing, as on the rest of the row (FLD-12). WHEN countText changes THE field SHALL draw the new text at once, without a motion.
behavior.verify: Fixtures text-stacked-counter, text-outlined-counter, text-stacked-code-multiline-counter and text-stacked-code-multiline-rtl, each given its countText by hand. Unit: with supportingText long enough to wrap, the count stays on the first line at the end and the text never comes closer than the counter's gap; the drawn count is not in the accessibility tree. Fixture text-stacked-supporting-error-counter: the count is on the supporting row's first line, and it does not move when error becomes true and the error text takes the help's place (under append: is drawn below the help).

behavior.text: WHILE its control reports that it refused what was entered — an entry error of the control's own (for one, a text input of type date, time or date-time committed half-filled, or with a date or a time that is not available, TXI-30) — THE field SHALL be in the error condition exactly as WHILE error is true (FLD-8): it SHALL draw its error parts, expose the control as invalid, and show as its error text (FLD-31) the words the control gives for the refusal — errorText WHILE the control gives none — in its supporting row, where any error text stands (FLD-7, FLD-31); WHILE the control gives no words and errorText is empty THE field SHALL draw no error text, SHALL still mark itself and in debug builds SHALL report a refusal that has no words. WHEN the report begins, or its words change, while focus is inside the field THE field SHALL announce the error text as FLD-9 says. WHEN the control withdraws the report THE field SHALL return at once to what error and errorText say. THE field SHALL NOT validate for the control, and SHALL forget the report WHEN the control is replaced (FLD-23).
behavior.verify: Entry error cannot be a snapshot fixture (it needs typing and a commit). Unit: in a Field around a date text input, fill the month and the day and leave the input: the Field shows invalidText as its error text, in its help's place where it has one, and the input is invalid; the next keystroke on a segment takes the error text away and draws the help where it was.

behavior.text: WHILE valueText is not empty and the label is drawn THE field SHALL draw valueText at the end edge of the label row, on the baseline of the label's first line, on one line, in comp.field.value-text.typescale and comp.field.standard.value-text.color (comp.field.standard.error.value-text.color WHILE error is true), and SHALL keep at least comp.field.value-text.gap between it and the label with its requirement mark: the label wraps in the room that is left (FLD-2) and the requirement tag moves to a line of its own as FLD-5 says. WHERE that leaves the label less than half of the row's width THE field SHALL instead draw the value text whole on a line of its own after the label row's last line, from the start edge, wrapping there where it must, and never cut. WHEN valueText changes THE field SHALL draw the new text at once, without a motion, and SHALL move no other part: the text is aligned to the end edge, so that only its own start moves. WHILE the label is not drawn THE field SHALL draw no value text, and it SHALL never draw one in the supporting row.
behavior.verify: Fixtures slider-value-text, slider-value-words, slider-range and slider-long-value-text. Unit: in a field 160 wide a value text that leaves the label less than half of the row is drawn whole on a line of its own after the label; with labelHidden no value text is drawn.

behavior.text: THE field SHALL keep the drawn value text from assistive technology and SHALL announce no change of it, because the control says its own value and a second reading would say it twice; a control that exposes no value is the product's to mend, not the frame's to speak for. A press on the value text SHALL do what a press on the label does (FLD-12). THE field SHALL NOT read, compute or format a value: valueText is words it is given.
behavior.verify: Unit: the value text is not in the accessibility tree and changing valueText announces nothing; a press on it moves focus to the control and changes no value.

behavior.text: WHILE the field is in error — error is true, or its control reports that it refused an entry (FLD-28) — and has words for it — errorText, or the control's own words for a refusal — THE field SHALL draw those words as its error text, in its supporting row: as the row's first line, comp.field.supporting-text.gap below the control — in the help's place WHERE comp.field.error-text.placement is replace (FLD-7), and WHILE supportingText is empty under either value — and WHERE it is append and supportingText is not empty, comp.field.error-text.gap below the last line of the help. It SHALL start where the help starts (FLD-26), be drawn in comp.field.supporting-text.typescale and comp.field.standard.error-text.color (its focused and disabled tokens as FLD-13 and FLD-14 say), wrap onto as many lines as it needs, never be cut, and never share a line with the help. WHILE the field is not in error, or is in error without words, THE field SHALL draw no error text and no gap for it and SHALL keep no room for one: under replace a field with a help is as tall in error as at rest while its error text takes as many lines as its help, under append it is taller by comp.field.error-text.gap and the lines of its error text, and a form at rest is no taller for errors it does not have. WHEN the error text appears, goes or changes its words THE field SHALL draw the row as it then is at once, with no motion of its own — what stands below the field moves with the layout, and only the colors of FLD-13 ease — so there is nothing here that reduced motion changes. THE field SHALL lay the error text out as text of its own direction (FLD-21), mirror it with its row (FLD-18), draw it in the platform's text color under forced colors (FLD-17), let it wrap and grow with enlarged text (FLD-16), and do nothing WHEN it is pressed (FLD-12).
behavior.verify: Fixtures text-stacked-supporting-error, text-outlined-supporting-error, text-stacked-supporting-error-long and text-stacked-supporting-error-rtl. Under the default system (replace), below the control: 4, one line of error text (16), and no help; the same field out of error draws its one line of help there and is as tall. With comp.field.error-text.placement append: 4, one line of help (16), 4, one line of error text (16); the same field out of error is 20 shorter, and its label, its control and its help are where they were. Unit: with supportingText empty the error text is 4 below the control, the picture every fixture named *-error without help had before this sentence; setting error to false removes the error text and its gap in the same frame; a field with error true and errorText empty draws its help in its resting place and color and no second line (fixture slider-error-without-text).

behavior.text: IF required and optional are both true THEN THE field SHALL behave as WHILE required alone is true — it draws the required mark and no optional tag, and says no optionalText — and in debug builds SHALL report that optional is ignored, because a control is never both required and optional.

accessibility.labeling: The field has no role of its own: it is a frame, and assistive technology meets the control. label is the control's accessible name, drawn or not (labelHidden), unless the control names itself. The control's description is what the supporting row draws — the help (supportingText) and, while the field is in error, the error text in its place or after it (FLD-11) — then optionalText while optional is true. The control is exposed as invalid while error is true, as required while required is true — whichever mark is drawn, and the mark itself is hidden — and as disabled while disabled is true. The label glyph is decorative.
notes: Not interactive by itself: the field takes no focus and adds no key (FLD-12), so it has no target of its own to size and minimumTarget holds through its control, whose own spec sizes its hit area. A press on the label moves focus to the control and never operates it; the label therefore widens where a pointer can land without widening what a press does.

There is one frame: a composed field — a text field — is this Field around its one control and draws no rows of its own. No component draws these rows itself; a composed field placed inside a field is reported (FLD-15).

Each platform carries the name, the description and the three states to the control in its own way, and a control the product built receives them the same way a Tanrei control does: on the web as ARIA attributes on the slotted element; in SwiftUI through the environment and the accessibility modifiers of the framed view; in Compose through a composition local and merged semantics; in Flutter through an inherited widget and a Semantics node around the control; in React Native through a context and the accessibility props of the wrapper.

Errors are words (WCAG 3.3.1, 1.4.1): errorText says what is wrong and how to put it right, the control is exposed as invalid, and the error color is one more sign, never the only one. The error text is announced when it appears under the person's focus and is otherwise read with the control (FLD-9); it never takes focus away.

After a failed submission a product should also say, above the form, how many answers were refused and link to each: that summary is a live Callout in its error status, not a part of any field. The field does not build it, because only the form knows all of its errors.

While the field is in error the error text takes the help's place under the default system (comp.field.error-text.placement replace): the one line below the control then says what is wrong, and a form in error is no taller than at rest; errorText should then also say how to put the answer right, because the help is not drawn. A design system that keeps the help in view while the person corrects the answer chooses append: the help stays and the error text is added below it, and a field with a help is taller in error by the error text and its gap. Under both, nothing above the error text moves, and no room is held open before an error exists. A field group keeps its description and gives its error a row of its own (FGR-7, FGR-8).
An asterisk alone does not explain itself: a product that marks required controls with an asterisk says what it means once, near the top of the form. The tag says it in words.
Heights are the texts': at 200% text size the label and the supporting row wrap and the field grows; nothing is cut (WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.10).
Forced colors (FLD-17): the error and the help then look alike, which is why the error must be in words and in the invalid state.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

A control can say three things back to its field, each by the same channel the field names it by: that it draws the label itself (FLD-25), where its content starts and ends (FLD-26) and a refusal of an entry (FLD-28). They are what makes a Field around a text input by hand the same picture as a text field; a control that says none of them is framed as before.

A place for words about the control's value is a prop of the field, named for what it holds: the field draws the words it is given, never reads, counts or formats a value, and keeps the drawn text from assistive technology, because the control says the same itself. countText is the first such place (FLD-27). A composed field fills it from its control (a text field, TXF-67); a product that writes the pair by hand writes it, at each change.

valueText is a place for words about the control's value (FLD-29, FLD-30): the field draws the words it is given at the end of the label row, never reads or formats a value, and keeps the drawn text from assistive technology, because the control says its own value. A slider field fills it from its slider (SLF-3); a product that writes the pair by hand writes it, at each change.

web.notes: `<tanrei-field label="Volume"><tanrei-slider></tanrei-slider></tanrei-field>`: the control is the one element in the default slot. It stays in the product's light DOM, so it keeps its place in a `<form>`, its `name` and `value`, its events and its styles; the field is not form-associated and holds no value. The label, the asterisk, the supporting row and the requirement tag (a `<tanrei-tag size="small">`, `filled` or `tonal`, `disabled` while the field is, with nothing else set on it: it reads the Tag's tokens as every tag where the field stands does) are in the shadow root; the label glyph is the `label-icon` slot. An id cannot be referenced across a shadow boundary, so the field does not point `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` at its own texts: it gives them as strings. A Tanrei control asks for them (it dispatches a composed `tanrei-field-connect` event when it is connected, the nearest field answers with `{ label, description, invalid, required, disabled }` and tells it of every change), writes them on its inner native element or role holder, and lets its own `label` win. Any other element receives `aria-label` (only where it has neither `aria-label` nor `aria-labelledby`), `aria-description`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and, where it has the property, `disabled`; the field removes exactly what it set when the element leaves the slot (`slotchange`, FLD-23). The announcement of FLD-9 is a visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` element in the shadow root, written only while `:focus-within` holds. A press on the label calls `focus()` on the control; `focusin` and `focusout` on the host select the focused tokens. Attributes are kebab-case: `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `required-mark`, `required-text`, `optional-text`. The host is `display: block`. Under `forced-colors: active` the texts are `CanvasText`. Words: the element has no words of its own. `required-text` and `optional-text` left empty read the product's words, set once with `setWords()` from `@tanrei/web`; the element draws again when they change. The exchange with a control runs both ways. Beside the name, the description and the three states, the field gives `labelHidden` and `requiredMark` (`asterisk` or `none`) to a control that draws the label itself; and a control may say `drawsLabel`, `inset: { start, end }` and `refusal: { text }` of itself through the same connection (FLD-25, FLD-26, FLD-28). A control that says none of them is framed as any other, and a field ignores what it does not know. The supporting row is a flex row whose `padding-inline` is the inset. The count is not in the exchange: `count-text` is an attribute of the field, drawn in a `part="counter"` element at the end of the supporting row, `aria-hidden`, `white-space: nowrap`, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (FLD-27). The supporting row holds two texts. `part="supporting-text"` is the help alone, not rendered while the error text stands in its place; `part="error-text"` is the error text — the row's first line under `replace`, a block below the help, `--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-gap` away, under `append` — in `--tanrei-comp-field-standard-error-text-color`, rendered only while the field is in error with words (FLD-31). The two are one column that takes the room beside the `counter` part, which is aligned to the first line. `--tanrei-comp-field-error-text-placement` is read by name (`replace`, the first, or `append`) from the cascade at each render, and the field draws again when the design system is switched. The `aria-description` the field gives its control is what the row draws (the help, the error text, or the two in that order) and the optional text, joined (FLD-11); the live region of FLD-9 is given the error text alone. `shownText()` of the frame does not choose between the two. The tag's element carries no custom property and is centred on the label's line without its height being read; `required-mark` takes `tag`; and `--tanrei-comp-field-requirement-mark` is `var(--tanrei-sys-behavior-requirement-mark)` until a layer sets it.

swiftui.notes: `TanreiField("Volume", supportingText:, errorText:, error:, required:, optional:) { TanreiSlider(value: $volume) }`, the glyph given by name through `labelIcon:`. `labelHidden` follows the `.labelsHidden()` environment and `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`, which also disables the content. The content is one view; the field sets `.accessibilityLabel`, `.accessibilityHint` (the description) and the invalid and required values on it, and offers the same values in the environment (`\.tanreiField`) for a control the product built. The product's words are read from the `\.tanreiWords` environment value. Not built on this platform yet: the supporting row is a `VStack` of the help and, in error, the error text — in the help's place, or `comp.field.error-text.gap` below it, as `comp.field.error-text.placement` names (FLD-7); the hint is what the row draws, then the optional text (FLD-11, FLD-31). Not built on this platform yet: the requirement tag as this platform's Tag at its small size with nothing of the field's set on it (FLD-5); generated tokens with none of the field's values for it and with the system's choice of mark, which the field's own token follows (FLD-6); the first mark named tag.

compose.notes: `TanreiField(label = "Volume", supportingText = …, isError = …, required = …, optional = …) { TanreiSlider(…) }`, the glyph given by name through `labelIcon`. `enabled` is the inverse flag and is offered to the content through `LocalTanreiFieldState`, with the name, the description and `isError`; Tanrei controls read it, and a control the product built reads the same composition local. The field adds `contentDescription`, `stateDescription` and `error(…)` to the merged semantics of its content. The product's words are read from `LocalTanreiWords`. Not built on this platform yet: the supporting row is a `Column` of the help and, in error, the error text — in the help's place, or `comp.field.error-text.gap` below it, as `comp.field.error-text.placement` names (FLD-7); the description offered through `LocalTanreiFieldState` is what the row draws, then the optional text (FLD-11, FLD-31). Not built on this platform yet: the requirement tag as this platform's Tag at its small size with nothing of the field's set on it (FLD-5); generated tokens with none of the field's values for it and with the system's choice of mark, which the field's own token follows (FLD-6); the first mark named tag.

flutter.notes: `TanreiField(labelText: 'Volume', helperText: …, errorText: …, isError: …, required: …, optional: …, child: TanreiSlider(…))`, the glyph given by name through `labelIcon`. `enabled` is the inverse flag. The names follow `InputDecoration`, as the text field's do. The field wraps its child in a `Semantics(label:, hint:, enabled:)` node and an inherited `TanreiFieldScope` that Tanrei controls and the product's own read. The product's words are read from the `TanreiWords` inherited widget, which the app fills from its own localizations. Not built on this platform yet: `errorText` takes the helper's place, as `InputDecoration`'s does, under `comp.field.error-text.placement` replace, and is drawn below `helperText`, which stays, `comp.field.error-text.gap` away, under append (FLD-7); the `Semantics` hint is what the row draws, then the optional text (FLD-11, FLD-31). Not built on this platform yet: the requirement tag as this platform's Tag at its small size with nothing of the field's set on it (FLD-5); generated tokens with none of the field's values for it and with the system's choice of mark, which the field's own token follows (FLD-6); the first mark named tag.

react-native.notes: `<Field label="Volume" supportingText="…"><Slider … /></Field>`; the glyph is the `labelIcon` prop (a glyph name). The one child receives the name, the description and the states through `FieldContext` (Tanrei controls read it; a control the product built calls `useField()`), and on Android the label is also tied with `accessibilityLabelledBy`. Follows the app's direction where an ancestor's is not known. The product's words are read from the `TanreiWordsProvider` context. Not built on this platform yet: the requirement tag as this platform's Tag at its small size with nothing of the field's set on it (FLD-5); generated tokens with none of the field's values for it and with the system's choice of mark, which the field's own token follows (FLD-6); the first mark named tag.
